panels.description: End-to-end task queue delivery latency: time from task scheduled (history) to worker picking it up (matching → worker). Healthy = low and stable. Rising p99 under shard contention means the server’s transfer queue is backing up.
panels.title: Schedule-to-Start Latency by Task Queue

panels.description: temporal_task_latency: time for the history service’s transfer-queue processor to handle one task (write to matching + persistence). Spikes here mean the history service is the bottleneck, not the workers. Correlated with shard I/O semaphore latency.
panels.title: Transfer Task Processing Latency (Server)

panels.description: Server-side resource exhausted errors: persistence-layer DB throttle (persistence_errors_resource_exhausted) and frontend/history/matching rate-limiter rejections. Under shard contention the persistence layer will start returning ResourceExhausted when the shard I/O queue depth is saturated.
panels.title: Resource Exhausted Errors — Server

panels.description: temporal_request: successful regular RPC calls from the SDK (worker + client). Break down by operation to see which calls are flowing. Under shard contention, RespondWorkflowTaskCompleted and RespondActivityTaskCompleted will slow down or fail.
panels.title: Request Rate by Operation

panels.description: temporal_request_failure: failed regular RPC calls, tagged by operation and status_code. Under shard contention watch for ResourceExhausted or DeadlineExceeded on RespondWorkflowTaskCompleted / RespondActivityTaskCompleted.
panels.title: Request Failure Rate by Operation

panels.description: temporal_request_latency: end-to-end latency of regular RPC calls as seen by the SDK. Shard I/O contention inflates RespondWorkflowTaskCompleted and RespondActivityTaskCompleted here — the gRPC call blocks until UpdateWorkflowExecution clears the semaphore.
panels.title: Request Latency by Operation

panels.description: temporal_long_request: successful long-poll calls (PollWorkflowTaskQueue, PollActivityTaskQueue). A drop here while failures rise means pollers are being shed — namespace rate limit being hit due to shard pressure propagating to the frontend.
panels.title: Long Request Rate by Operation

panels.description: temporal_long_request_failure: failed long-poll calls. PollWorkflowTaskQueue and PollActivityTaskQueue are the lowest priority in the execution rate limit bucket — they're the first to be shed when the server is under pressure.
panels.title: Long Request Failure Rate by Operation

panels.description: temporal_long_request_latency: end-to-end latency of long-poll calls. Normally ~1m (poll timeout) for empty polls. Spikes below 1m mean polls are returning early with errors. Drops toward 0 mean polls are failing immediately.
panels.title: Long Request Latency

panels.description: Time from when a task is scheduled (shard writes it) to when a worker picks it up. Under shard contention the scheduling step itself is delayed — so this latency rises even if workers have free pollers. This is the clearest cross-layer signal linking shard I/O pressure to worker impact.
panels.title: Schedule-to-Start Latency (Workflow Task & Activity)

panels.description: temporal_worker_task_slots_available: free execution slots on the worker, by worker_type (WorkflowWorker / ActivityWorker). Should stay well above zero — if this reaches 0 the worker is the bottleneck, not the server. Use this to confirm shards are the constraint, not the workers.
panels.title: Worker Task Slots Available

panels.description: Time spent waiting to acquire the shard I/O semaphore. Each shard has shardIOConcurrency slots (default 1). With 4 shards and many concurrent workflows, operations queue here first.
panels.title: Semaphore Latency

panels.description: semaphore_requests: total acquisition attempts per second. semaphore_failures: failed acquisitions (context cancelled / timed out). Non-zero failures = workflows being dropped.
panels.title: Semaphore Requests & Failures (rate)

panels.description: Time waiting for the shard read/write lock — acquired after the semaphore, inside UpdateWorkflowExecution / CreateWorkflowExecution. Rises in tandem with semaphore_latency under contention.
panels.title: Shard Lock Latency

panels.description: Cumulative semaphore_failures. Any non-zero value means a shard I/O operation was dropped — the caller's context was cancelled before it could acquire a slot. Watch for this going non-zero under load.
panels.title: Semaphore Failures (total counter)

panels.description: dd_shard_io_semaphore_latency: deadlock detector's view of how long threads are stuck waiting on the shard I/O semaphore. Fires before an actual deadlock — sustained high values here are a leading indicator that shards are saturated. Complements semaphore_latency from Tier 1.
panels.title: DD — Shard I/O Semaphore Latency

panels.description: dd_shard_lock_latency: deadlock detector's view of time spent waiting for the shard read/write lock. Rises alongside semaphore contention since the lock is acquired inside the semaphore. A separate signal from the I/O semaphore — both should spike together under contention.
panels.title: DD — Shard Lock Latency

panels.description: dd_shard_controller_lock_latency: deadlock detector's view of the shard controller lock. The controller lock gates shard acquisition and removal — spikes here indicate contention at the cluster membership level, often a sign of shard rebalancing or thundering-herd re-acquisition after a restart.
panels.title: DD — Shard Controller Lock Latency

panels.description: persistence_latency{service_name="history"}: end-to-end DB call latency per operation. Under shard contention, UpdateWorkflowExecution and CreateWorkflowExecution rise because operations queue behind the semaphore. GetWorkflowExecution spikes indicate cache misses forcing DB reads on hot shards.
panels.title: Persistence Latency by Operation (History)

panels.description: persistence_errors_resource_exhausted{service_name="history"}: persistence calls rejected because persistenceMaxQPS was hit. Non-zero here means the shard is not just slow but actively being throttled at the DB layer — a secondary effect of hot shards generating too many writes.
panels.title: Persistence Resource Exhausted Errors (History)

panels.description: persistence_shard_rps: histogram of per-shard persistence RPS. With 4 shards and uneven hashing, a few buckets will carry disproportionate load. A heavily skewed distribution (long tail) confirms hot-shard contention rather than uniform load.
panels.title: Persistence RPS per Shard (Distribution)

panels.description: shardinfo_immediate_queue_lag: difference between the smallest pending immediate task ID and the last generated task ID per shard. Grows when the history service cannot process tasks (transfer, visibility, replication) as fast as they are being created. A rising lag here is a direct measure of how backed-up hot shards are.
panels.title: Shard Immediate Queue Lag

panels.description: shardinfo_scheduled_queue_lag: difference between the earliest scheduled (timer) task fire time and now. Grows when the timer queue falls behind — timers fire later than intended. Under shard contention, timer tasks compete with transfer tasks for the same serialized shard write slot.
panels.title: Shard Scheduled Queue Lag

panels.description: pending_tasks: in-memory pending history tasks per shard. Tasks are loaded into memory from the DB and queued for execution. A growing count means the shard executor is falling behind. With 4 shards, this accumulates quickly on hot shards when the semaphore is saturated.
panels.title: Pending Tasks (In-Memory, per Shard)

panels.description: task_processing_no_persistence_latency: time spent processing a history task minus the time spent in DB calls. If this stays flat while persistence_latency and semaphore_latency spike, the bottleneck is purely I/O — not CPU or business logic. This confirms shard contention rather than compute pressure.
panels.title: Task Processing Latency (Excluding Persistence)

panels.description: acquire_lock_failed: count of times a workflow execution's mutable state lock could not be acquired within cacheNonUserContextLockTimeout (default 500ms). Happens when multiple concurrent operations target the same workflow and the shard is already slow. Non-zero = workflows actively dropping operations under contention.
panels.title: Workflow Lock Acquisition Failures

panels.description: numshards_gauge: number of shards currently owned by this history pod. With 4 shards on a single-node cluster this should be 4. Drops indicate shard loss (ownership moved elsewhere). Watch for sudden changes during load — shard rebalancing mid-test will confound results.
panels.title: Shards Owned per Pod

panels.description: sharditem_created_count and sharditem_removed_count: rate of shard context creation and removal. Should be near-zero during a stable test. Any churn mid-scenario means shards are being reacquired — often triggered by ownership loss under load, which will distort other shard metrics.
panels.title: Shard Churn (Created / Removed)

panels.description: get_engine_for_shard_latency: time to look up or initialize the engine for a shard on an incoming request. Normally fast (cached). Spikes indicate the engine was not resident — either shard was just acquired or evicted — adding cold-start latency on top of regular contention.
panels.title: Get Engine for Shard Latency
